text:
maya: Quick design review thread — uploaded new Figma for compact compare + filters hierarchy, see attachment and notes. looking for: filter affordances, pin behavior on version rows, and badge semantics. https://figma.local/compact-compare (mock)
kai: thanks — can we start with filter hierarchy? i worry nested filters are easy to miss on small screens. suggestion: collapse parent by default and show count badge for children.
sanjay: implementation note — collapsing parent and lazy-rendering children is straightforward. the counts will need an extra endpoint or precomputed facet counts. extra RT ~20ms/req if we calc on the fly.
olivia: accessibility nits:
- badges need text alternatives (screen readers should read "196 models matching" not just a color)
- pin icon should have a clear aria-label and keyboard focus state
example: `<button aria-label="Pin model version 1.3, not pinned">` or `aria-pressed` toggles.
ben: +1 on counts being precomputed. live counts on every keystroke will blow up DB queries. can we debounce and show a spinner on filter chip while loading?
maya: good call. i'll change the interaction: debounce 300ms, show grey placeholder count, then update. also adding a tooltip: "approximate count — refresh after filters applied".
emma: copy suggestions for pin modal: current: "Pin this version" -> proposed: "Pin version to keep it fixed for compare and rollouts". shorter inline label: just "Pin" on the row, full text in tooltip.
olivia: contrast concern on performance badges: green on light green is low contrast at 12px. recommend darker tones and an icon fallback for colorblind: `✓` for good, `!` for degraded.
sanjay: for badges we should use CSS variables so product can tweak: `--badge-good: #166534` `--badge-warn: #b45309` ; icons as svgs to keep size small.
maya: question on pinning UX: should pin be per-compare-row (persist per-user) or global per-catalog? Product decision.
kai: prefer per-user pinned versions for compare views. enterprise might want org-level pin later but start with user-scoped.
ben: engineering note: store a small user preference object `{pinned_versions: {catalog_id: version_id}}` — cheap and simple.
maya: flow decision: clicking pin immediately pins (optimistic update). show snackbar "Pinned version 1.3 — undo". if save fails, revert and show inline error.
emma: UX copy for snackbar: "Pinned version 1.3 for this catalog. Undo" — ok?
olivia: add screen reader announcement: "Version 1.3 pinned" when action completes.
design-bot: exported frame "compare_v4_filters_hierarchy" to project "catalog-ui" by maya at 2026-03-22T10:02Z :pushpin: 
maya: updated frame based on feedback: reduced badge size, darker badge palette, added aria-label examples in notes, debounce on filter counts, optimistic pin flow with undo.
kai: ok lets merge these into the final PR checklist:
- precompute facet counts or debounce + placeholder
- aria-labels for badges and pin (examples in figma notes)
- keyboard nav: left/right to move within row, enter/space to toggle pin
- badge color variables + svg icons
- optimistic pin w/ undo + analytics event `pin_version` (include catalog_id, version_id)
sanjay: i'll estimate work: 3 dev days + 1 day QA + 0.5 day a11y pass.
ben: schedule sprint ticket and mark as medium priority.
maya: thanks all — i'll push an updated figma link and add the checklist items to the ticket. :thumbsup: 
kai: small follow-up — can we keep the compare table row density option (compact/comfortable) for power users? important for customers with long lists.
maya: yes, adding a toggle in the toolbar. will mock both states.
olivia: final a11y checklist reminder: focus outline visible, reachable via keyboard, aria-live announcements for snackbar, badges read as text + icon.
emma: copy doc link: https://docs.internal/copy/pinning-and-badges — will update lines after maya finalizes.
maya: end — will ping when figma updated. :sparkles:
